summary: A native checkbox with the system's styling, supporting an indeterminate state.
useWhen: a single on/off choice inside a form that is submitted
several independent options where more than one may be picked

useInstead.when: the change takes effect immediately rather than on submit
useInstead.why: a switch reads as a setting taking effect now; a checkbox reads as a value being collected

useInstead.when: there are many options and space is tight

lg.use: touch targets and prominent single choices

neutral.use: where the checked state is a fact rather than an approval — bulk-selection columns

danger.use: consenting to something destructive or irreversible

children.note: the visible label; omit for a bare box and supply `aria-label` instead

guarantees: a real <input type="checkbox">, so form association, label clicking, and correct announcement come from the platform
`isIndeterminate` is written to the DOM property after every render — HTML has no such attribute, so React cannot set it declaratively
requires: `children`, or `aria-label` when the box has no visible label — a row-selection checkbox always needs one

antiPatterns.dont: a bare checkbox with no `children` and no `aria-label`
antiPatterns.why: every row announces an unnamed checkbox
indeterminate means "some of my children are checked"; on a leaf it is a state the user can never reach
form association, the indeterminate property and label clicking are not free to reimplement
